profiles.title: Communication
profiles.setting: the media room at a school in Sohar
profiles.challenge: messages were misunderstood when short captions lacked context
profiles.evidence: a comparison of the original audio and two rewritten captions
profiles.solution: a peer-review checklist for captions and respectful replies
profiles.result: families understood the new bilingual bulletin more easily
profiles.future: a workshop on clear spoken and written messages
profiles.material: a microphone and a shared editing computer
profiles.counterpoint: some families preferred printed notices to phone messages
profiles.ethic: asking speakers for permission before publishing their voices
profiles.debate: Schools should replace printed notices with digital messages
profiles.pro: online notices can be corrected quickly and reach pupils who are absent
profiles.con: some families cannot check a phone regularly and a short message may be misunderstood
profiles.lesson: clear communication depends on checking meaning rather than simply sending more messages
profiles.grammar: present simple, present continuous, modal suggestions
profiles.storyIssue: a meeting notice appeared with the correct day but the wrong room
profiles.storyAction: she compared the notice with the booking records and spoke to the organiser
profiles.storyOutcome: the team used one official noticeboard and a matching website update

profiles.title: Travellers and Tourists
profiles.challenge: visitors overlooked local customs and damaged small footpaths
profiles.evidence: visitor feedback forms and photographs of worn sections of the route
profiles.solution: clear bilingual signs and smaller guided groups
profiles.result: visitors stayed on marked paths and asked more respectful questions
profiles.future: a cultural walking map created with village residents
profiles.material: a printed route map and reusable water bottles
profiles.counterpoint: some travellers wanted more time to explore independently
profiles.ethic: obtaining permission before photographing residents and homes
profiles.debate: Guided village tours are better than independent visits
profiles.pro: local guides provide accurate cultural knowledge and protect sensitive places
profiles.con: some visitors prefer flexibility and the cost of a guide may discourage families
profiles.lesson: good tourism respects communities as well as the interests of visitors
profiles.storyIssue: a visiting group arrived after the route had changed because of heavy rain
profiles.storyAction: she contacted the guide and arranged an accessible alternative
profiles.storyOutcome: visitors reached the craft workshop safely and learned about local traditions

profiles.title: Innovation
profiles.setting: the science laboratory at a school in Sohar
profiles.challenge: a leaking tap wasted water when nobody noticed it
profiles.evidence: two weeks of observations and readings from a moisture sensor
profiles.solution: a warning light that alerts staff when water continues flowing unusually long
profiles.result: fewer unnoticed leaks were reported during the final trial
profiles.future: a student exhibition with open instructions for other schools
profiles.material: a battery-powered sensor and recycled plastic housing
profiles.counterpoint: some pupils suggested buying an expensive automatic valve instead
profiles.ethic: testing the device safely without leaving electrical parts near standing water
profiles.debate: Students should build low-cost prototypes rather than buy ready-made technology
profiles.pro: building prototypes develops problem-solving skills and offers affordable local solutions
profiles.con: some devices require professional testing and a commercial system may be more reliable
profiles.lesson: innovation means careful testing and improvement, not simply a clever idea
profiles.storyIssue: the first sensor gave a false warning after a cleaning accident
profiles.storyAction: he checked the readings and redesigned the protective cover
profiles.storyOutcome: the revised device worked more reliably and was demonstrated at the school fair

profiles.title: In the Past
profiles.topic: a collection of family recipes and oral histories
profiles.challenge: older recipes included measurements that younger readers could not recognise
profiles.evidence: handwritten notebooks compared with interviews of older family members
profiles.solution: bilingual captions explaining original measures without changing historical meaning
profiles.result: visitors understood how everyday family life had changed over generations
profiles.future: a digital collection of consented stories and photographs
profiles.material: a borrowed microphone and copies of handwritten recipes
profiles.counterpoint: some visitors preferred modern versions of old recipes
profiles.ethic: labelling undated photographs honestly instead of inventing dates
profiles.debate: Schools should preserve family objects rather than focus only on famous historical events
profiles.pro: ordinary objects reveal valuable evidence about food, work and family relationships
profiles.con: records may be incomplete and storing delicate objects requires time and resources
profiles.lesson: historical research requires comparing evidence and acknowledging uncertainty
profiles.storyIssue: her grandmother's notebook contained an unfamiliar word for a traditional cooking measure
profiles.storyAction: she interviewed two neighbours and compared their explanations with other records
profiles.storyOutcome: the team produced a corrected exhibition label that preserved the original wording

profiles.title: Careers
profiles.topic: a careers discovery fair for school leavers
profiles.challenge: many teenagers assumed a job title told them everything about daily responsibilities
profiles.evidence: interviews with a designer, a nurse and a renewable-energy technician
profiles.solution: practical task stations and questions about real working routines
profiles.result: students identified skills they could develop before leaving school
profiles.future: short mentoring meetings with local employers
profiles.material: occupation cards and example interview questions
profiles.counterpoint: some students wanted information about university fees before choosing a path
profiles.ethic: presenting every career respectfully without ranking jobs by social status
profiles.debate: Career education should begin before the final year of school
profiles.pro: early exploration helps pupils connect personal strengths with study choices
profiles.con: teenagers' interests may change and premature labels can restrict confidence
profiles.lesson: career decisions develop through evidence, reflection and real conversations
profiles.storyIssue: he prepared for a job interview by memorising answers that did not match his own experience
profiles.storyAction: a mentor helped him describe authentic examples of teamwork and problem solving
profiles.storyOutcome: he answered questions confidently and planned useful training for next year

profiles.title: Starting University
profiles.topic: a peer-support orientation for first-year university students
profiles.challenge: new students were confused about timetables, campus facilities and independent study
profiles.evidence: anonymous orientation surveys and questions submitted by new arrivals
profiles.solution: a peer-mentor map and practical sessions on planning a weekly timetable
profiles.result: participants found their classrooms and study support services more confidently
profiles.future: a monthly mentoring meeting and online guidance pages
profiles.material: a campus map and sample university timetable
profiles.counterpoint: some students preferred to ask for help online rather than in large groups
profiles.ethic: keeping personal accommodation and financial concerns confidential
profiles.debate: New university students should live on campus rather than at home
profiles.pro: campus accommodation can build independence and make study facilities easier to reach
profiles.con: living at home may reduce costs and provide important family support
profiles.lesson: starting university involves learning to ask questions and manage responsibilities
profiles.grammar: past perfect and sequence of events
profiles.storyIssue: she discovered on arrival that her course timetable had changed after she printed it
profiles.storyAction: she contacted her adviser and updated her weekly plan before the first lecture
profiles.storyOutcome: she found the correct room and helped two other new students

profiles.title: Tourism and Hospitality
profiles.topic: an accessible welcome programme for visitors
profiles.challenge: guests struggled to understand excursion information and some needed step-free access
profiles.evidence: visitor comments, route inspections and a review of reception questions
profiles.solution: clear multilingual guidance and a revised accessible tour timetable
profiles.result: guests could choose suitable activities and staff handled questions more confidently
profiles.future: a community-led guide to responsible tourism in Dhofar
profiles.material: an accessible map and multilingual welcome cards
profiles.counterpoint: some travellers preferred independent routes with no fixed schedule
profiles.ethic: protecting personal information and respecting local cultural practices
profiles.debate: Hotels should invest more in training local guides than in advertising
profiles.pro: qualified local guides improve visitor experiences and support community employment
profiles.con: advertising can attract new visitors and training requires time and money
profiles.lesson: good hospitality combines clear information, inclusion and respect for visitors
profiles.storyIssue: a visitor's excursion was cancelled when a mountain road became unsafe after rain
profiles.storyAction: he explained the options calmly and organised a safer coastal alternative
profiles.storyOutcome: the group enjoyed the day and thanked the staff for honest advice

profiles.title: Travel and Transport
profiles.challenge: students had missed appointments after unexpected bus delays
profiles.evidence: a month of journey logs comparing waiting times on different routes
profiles.solution: updated information boards and a tested shared transport schedule
profiles.result: commuters could plan more reliable connections and communicate changes early
profiles.future: a small mobile timetable with accessibility information
profiles.material: a route map and anonymised journey logs
profiles.counterpoint: some families still preferred private cars because of their flexibility
profiles.ethic: avoiding publication of individual students' travel locations
profiles.debate: Public transport should be prioritised over additional private parking near schools
profiles.pro: shared routes can reduce congestion and improve access for people without cars
profiles.con: routes need reliable timing and not every area has suitable connections
profiles.lesson: transport decisions require reliable evidence, safety and consideration for different travellers
profiles.grammar: present perfect and present perfect continuous, for and since
profiles.storyIssue: his bus had been delayed for several weeks because of road repairs
profiles.storyAction: he recorded the journey times and discussed alternatives with the transport office
profiles.storyOutcome: the service introduced clearer announcements and a more dependable connection
